evidence.claim: Frequent changes in monetary policy, epitomized by rate cuts since September 2021, sent the lira to historic lows and inflation to record highs, and these challenges eroded real incomes for poorer households.
evidence.title: Global and Domestic Challenges Weigh on Outlook for Turkish Economy in 2022
evidence.excerpt: Frequent changes in monetary policy, epitomized by rate cuts since September 2021, sent the lira to historic lows and inflation to record highs, and these challenges eroded real incomes for poorer households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct World Bank country press release with a concrete, dated claim about policy, currency, inflation, and household welfare.
evidence.period_fit: Targets the 2022 outlook and directly describes the policy environment entering 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdogan because the rate-cut policy and monetary stance were his signature economic choices.
contrary_evidence: The same release notes exports had grown strongly in 2021 and remained part of the growth story.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Turkey was experiencing rising macro-financial volatility with impacts on households and that tighter monetary policy was warranted to restore investor confidence and anchor inflation expectations.
evidence.title: Turkey Economic Monitor: Sailing Against the Tide
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Turkey was experiencing rising macro-financial volatility with impacts on households and that tighter monetary policy was warranted to restore investor confidence and anchor inflation expectations.
evidence.source_locator: story highlights and taking stock section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct World Bank country monitor with a clear policy assessment and household-impact framing.
evidence.period_fit: Early-2022 snapshot of the ruler-period and its inherited macro position.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Erdogan government as the policy environment under review, though this is partly a baseline assessment rather than a discrete 2022 decision record.
contrary_evidence: The monitor also noted a strong 2021 rebound in output and exports.

evidence.claim: Employment had recovered to pre-pandemic levels and income had been boosted by a 50% minimum wage increase, but prices were rising further because of accommodative monetary policy, commodity prices, and exchange-rate depreciation, eroding real incomes.
evidence.title: Türkiye: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 1
evidence.excerpt: Employment had recovered to pre-pandemic levels and income had been boosted by a 50% minimum wage increase, but prices were rising further because of accommodative monetary policy, commodity prices, and exchange-rate depreciation, eroding real incomes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD surveillance text with specific labor, wage, inflation, and policy statements for the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 economic conditions and policy mix.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdogan because the accommodative monetary stance was the government-backed framework in place during 2022.
contrary_evidence: The minimum wage increase provided some near-term household support.

evidence.claim: Real GDP grew by 7.5% in the first half of 2022, tourism fully recovered, and exporters benefited from supply-chain disruption, but investment remained subdued and macroeconomic imbalances rose.
evidence.title: Türkiye: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 2
evidence.excerpt: Real GDP grew by 7.5% in the first half of 2022, tourism fully recovered, and exporters benefited from supply-chain disruption, but investment remained subdued and macroeconomic imbalances rose.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD country surveillance with specific 2022 growth, tourism, investment, and imbalance data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Erdogan because the policy environment shaped investment and stabilization conditions, though some of the growth was externally driven.
contrary_evidence: The same passage says investment activity was subdued and imbalances rose.

evidence.claim: Consumer price inflation reached 85.5% and producer price inflation 158% by October 2022, while the minimum wage was raised by 30% in July after a 50% increase and lira depreciation raised import-price pressures.
evidence.title: Türkiye: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 2
evidence.excerpt: Consumer price inflation reached 85.5% and producer price inflation 158% by October 2022, while the minimum wage was raised by 30% in July after a 50% increase and lira depreciation raised import-price pressures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD gives concrete inflation and wage figures for the target year, tied to policy and exchange-rate conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdogan-era macro policy because the inflation and depreciation sit within the low-rate regime he defended.
contrary_evidence: The minimum-wage increase modestly cushioned purchasing power.

evidence.claim: The government introduced measures to shield vulnerable groups from rising energy and food prices, including doubled energy assistance for 4 million households and lower electricity tariffs for low-consumption users.
evidence.title: Türkiye: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 2
evidence.excerpt: The government introduced measures to shield vulnerable groups from rising energy and food prices, including doubled energy assistance for 4 million households and lower electricity tariffs for low-consumption users.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD country surveillance with specific distributional relief measures and household counts.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 policy response to the cost-of-living shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Erdogan government because it was a state response during his tenure, though it is mitigation rather than structural reform.
contrary_evidence: The same report warns that non-targeted price supports and energy dependence kept fiscal and inflation risks high.

evidence.claim: The IMF mission said policy-rate cuts in late 2021 added to existing vulnerabilities, were followed by lira depreciation and high inflation, and that it recommended early policy-rate hikes and stronger central-bank independence.
evidence.title: IMF Staff Completes 2022 Article IV Mission to Turkiye
evidence.excerpt: The IMF mission said policy-rate cuts in late 2021 added to existing vulnerabilities, were followed by lira depreciation and high inflation, and that it recommended early policy-rate hikes and stronger central-bank independence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous IMF mission statement, directly targeted to the 2022 consultation and policy mix.
evidence.period_fit: Direct target-period consultation statement from late 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdogan because the rate-cut path and institutional stance were government-driven policy choices.
contrary_evidence: The statement also notes strong post-pandemic growth and a dynamic private sector.

evidence.claim: The IMF summarized the new policy model as relying on low interest rates, directing lending to selected sectors, and increasingly distortionary macrofinancial and regulatory measures after the lira ran under severe pressure; it also said inflation reached 85% in October 2022 and fiscal risks were rising.
evidence.title: Republic of Turkiye: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The IMF summarized the new policy model as relying on low interest rates, directing lending to selected sectors, and increasingly distortionary macrofinancial and regulatory measures after the lira ran under severe pressure; it also said inflation reached 85% in October 2022 and fiscal risks were rising.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF country report with a concise synthesis of the 2022 policy model, its consequences, and associated risks.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but still about the 2022 consultation and 2022 outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdogan because the low-rate model, directed credit, and intervention-heavy response were core government choices.
contrary_evidence: The same summary notes the public-debt burden remained low compared with peers.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Nureddin Nebati, chosen by Erdogan to oversee and articulate the low-rate policy, had little direct economic training and replaced the last prominent orthodox-policy figure in the cabinet.
evidence.title: Turkey's new finance minister in the eye of a storm
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Nureddin Nebati, chosen by Erdogan to oversee and articulate the low-rate policy, had little direct economic training and replaced the last prominent orthodox-policy figure in the cabinet.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is contemporaneous and specific, though the mirror is secondary hosting rather than the wire itself.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to the ruler-period economic team.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong attribution to Erdogan because the appointment was his and it signaled the type of economic team he preferred.
contrary_evidence: Supporters said Nebati was working closely with the president and had helped stem the lira collapse.

evidence.claim: Erdogan repeated that interest rates would be lowered further and that inflation would fall as a result, describing the economic shock as temporary even as Turkey was in a currency crisis.
evidence.title: Erdogan says interest rates will be lowered and inflation will fall too
evidence.excerpt: Erdogan repeated that interest rates would be lowered further and that inflation would fall as a result, describing the economic shock as temporary even as Turkey was in a currency crisis.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters wire text in article body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters wire reporting, but accessed through a syndication mirror.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler attribution because the quote is Erdogan's own public economic guidance.
contrary_evidence: The article notes the central bank had already slashed rates 500 basis points since September and inflation was nearing a 20-year high.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Erdogan's bet that Turkey could ride out the inflation and currency shock with low rates and reserves had collapsed after the Ukraine war left the economy vulnerable to soaring energy prices, and that he was betting lower rates would reverse chronic trade deficits through exports and tourism.
evidence.title: Analysis-Fallout of Ukraine war exposes Turkey's vulnerable economy
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Erdogan's bet that Turkey could ride out the inflation and currency shock with low rates and reserves had collapsed after the Ukraine war left the economy vulnerable to soaring energy prices, and that he was betting lower rates would reverse chronic trade deficits through exports and tourism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters analysis with clear causal claims and explicit attribution to Erdogan's policy bet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdogan because the policy bet and rate-cut logic are explicitly described as his.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes costly market interventions and deposit protections briefly stabilized the lira in January.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 Turkish nuclear command-and-control or custody evidence is absent; the dossier mostly shows inherited treaty/NATO/IAEA posture plus civil-nuclear and mediation choices.
Direct forensic or documentary proof of Erdoğan's own assets, beneficial ownership, or personal enrichment in 2022 is still missing.
Independent corroboration beyond Reuters-style reporting is still thin for the media-control and family-access claims.
Audit-grade verification of project delivery and personnel effects is still thin; the package leans heavily on official program documents and self-reported completion counts.
